0:03. Fifteen seconds. Name only; the motivation is the next slide.

Thirty seconds. The room already agrees. Do not belabor it.
One incident, one slide, primary sources only. If task 9 is not done, cut this slide.

Re-verify the preview status in March 2027. Say 'adopt it when you can' out loud. Naming the platform answer early earns the next ten minutes.

Methodology before the number, so nobody has to ask. Mention the 100-star floor here and again on the deflating slide.
The centerpiece. Pause after the number.

Volunteer the inverse before a hostile questioner computes it. Do not call the rest clean.
Twenty seconds. Self-implicating detail; it buys credibility for the tool table that follows.
Neutral framing. ratchet is near-complete on GitHub Actions; say so. The disclosure is on the slide; read it.
0:17. Frame it as: here is concretely why GitHub put a run-time identity check in the lockfile.
Quote GitHub's own docs; this is documented behavior, not a discovery. The contribution is showing what the one sentence means in practice.
Live only if the network cooperates; cut to the recording without apologizing. Prefer the pre-commit variant: one demo carries both halves of the talk.
Ask the room what they would have caught. Nobody catches it; that is the point.
Claim only behavior observed in task 7. Keep the qualified wording: 'tools I reviewed'.
Say the limitation out loud. Honesty here is what separates this from a product pitch.
0:23. Shift from what is exposed to what it costs to fix.
One minute. Recommend all three before any third-party tool. Immutable releases are a publisher control: you cannot require them of the actions you consume. Re-verify all three in March 2027.
Replace <digest> only with a digest resolved during rehearsal; never invent one.
Anticipates the 'digest pins miss security patches' question. The answer is pin plus automated updates, with a deliberate cooldown.
Fill from the public-corpus dry run only. If task 17 is not done, cut this slide and give the time to Q&A.
Complementary layers, not competitors.
Thirty seconds. Leave it up long enough to photograph. These commands were tested on a fixture on 2026-10-25; re-run them before the talk.
0:33. The slide people photograph. Leave it up for a beat.
Twenty seconds. One URL matters: the published scanner and data.
